original: gandharvais tu mahārāja bhagne karṇe mahārathe / saṃprādravac camūḥ sarvā dhārtarāṣṭrasya paśyataḥ

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: Vaisampayana said, 'After that great warrior Karna had been routed by the Gandharvas, the entire Dhartarashtra army, O king, fled in all directions from fear.'

original: tān dṛṣṭvā dravataḥ sarvān dhārtarāṣṭrān parāṅmukhān / duryodhano mahārāja nāsīt tatra parāṅmukhaḥ

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: And beholding his army thus flying away with their faces turned from the field, Duryodhana alone, O monarch, did not flee from that spot.

original: tām āpatantīṃ saṃprekṣya gandharvāṇāṃ mahācamūm / mahatā śaravarṣeṇa so 'bhyavarṣad ariṃdamaḥ

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: And beholding the Gandharva host rushing impetuously towards him, that subduer of foes checked them with a mighty shower of arrows.

original: acintya śaravarṣaṃ tu gandharvās tasya taṃ ratham / duryodhanaṃ jighāṃsantaḥ samantāt paryavārayan

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: And those Gandharvas then, desirous of slaying Duryodhana, surrounded him on all sides, completely covering his car with a shower of shafts.

original: yugam īṣāṃ varūthaṃ ca tathaiva dhvajasārathī / aśvāṃs triveṇuṃ talpaṃ ca tilaśo 'bhyahanan ratham

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: And they then cut down his yoke, and his flagstaff, and his steeds, and his charioteer, and his car, into fragments.

original: duryodhanaṃ citraseno virathaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi / abhidrutya mahābāhur jīvagrāham athāgrahīt

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: And Chitrasena then, rushing impetuously towards Duryodhana who had fallen on the ground, seized him alive, even as the mighty Garuda seizeth a snake.

original: tasmin gṛhīte rājendra sthitaṃ duḥśāsanaṃ rathe / paryagṛhṇanta gandharvāḥ parivārya samantataḥ

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: And while the king was being thus taken away, Dushasana, who was seated on his car, was also seized by the Gandharvas.

original: viviṃśatiṃ citrasenam ādāyānye pradudruvuḥ / vindānuvindāv apare rājadārāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: And Vivinsati and Chitrasena, and the wives of the king, were also seized by others among those Gandharvas.

original: sainyās tu dhārtarāṣṭrasya gandharvaiḥ samabhidrutāḥ / pūrvaṃ prabhagnaiḥ sahitāḥ pāṇḍavān abhyayus tadā

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: And the troops of Dhritarashtra's son, fleeing away, O king, approached Yudhishthira, desirous of effecting the release of the king.

original: śakaṭāpaṇaveśyāś ca yānayugyaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ / śaraṇaṃ pāṇḍavāñ jagmur hriyamāṇe mahīpatau

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: Crying thus, the followers of Duryodhana, afflicted with grief and melancholy, approached Yudhishthira.

original: priyadarśano mahābāhur dhārtarāṣṭro mahābalaḥ / gandharvair hriyate rājā pārthās tam anudhāvata

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: Bhima then answered those old attendants of Duryodhana, saying, 'What we should have done with great efforts, arraying ourselves in line of battle...'

original: duḥśāsano durviṣaho durmukho durjayas tathā / baddhvā hriyante gandharvai rājadārāś ca sarvaśaḥ

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: ...supported by horses and elephants hath, indeed, been done by the Gandharvas. And while Bhima, the son of Kunti, was speaking thus in a voice of sarcasm, king Yudhishthira told him, 'This is not time for cruel words!'

original: iti duryodhanāmātyāḥ krośanto rājagṛddhinaḥ / ārtā dīnasvarāḥ sarve yudhiṣṭhiram upāgaman

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: The narrative describes the aftermath of the battle and the capture of Duryodhana by the Gandharvas. The followers of Duryodhana recount the events of the devastating defeat and plead for rescue from the Pandavas.

original: tāṃs tathā vyathitān dīnān bhikṣamāṇān yudhiṣṭhiram / vṛddhān duryodhanāmātyān bhīmaseno 'bhyabhāṣata

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: They approached Yudhishthira with great sorrow, recounting how the celestial Gandharvas easily defeated the Kaurava forces and captured their king.

original: anyathā vartamānānām artho jāto 'yam anyathā / asmābhir yad anuṣṭheyaṃ gandharvais tad anuṣṭhitam

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: The followers detailed the destruction of the Kuru army, emphasizing that even the mighty warriors like Karna could not withstand the Gandharvas' assault.

original: durmantritam idaṃ tāta rājño durdyūtadevinaḥ / dveṣṭāram anye klībasya pātayantīti naḥ śrutam

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: They pleaded with the Pandavas to set aside past enmities and rescue their cousin Duryodhana from the captivity of the Gandharva king Chitrasena.

original: tad idaṃ kṛtaṃ naḥ pratyakṣaṃ gandharvair atimānuṣam / diṣṭyā loke pumān asti kaś cid asmatpriye sthitaḥ / yenāsmākaṃ hṛto bhāra āsīnānāṃ sukhāvahaḥ

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: Bhima, hearing their pleas, could not hide his amusement and responded with sarcasm regarding the sudden turn of events.

original: śītavātātapasahāṃs tapasā caiva karśitān / samastho viṣamasthān hi draṣṭum icchati durmatiḥ

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: Bhima reminded them that what the Pandavas were preparing to do with great effort, the Gandharvas had accomplished effortlessly.

original: adharmacāriṇas tasya kauravyasya durātmanaḥ / ye śīlam anuvartante te paśyanti parābhavam

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: He pointed out the irony of the situation, where the very people who sought to humiliate the Pandavas were now seeking their protection.

original: adharmo hi kṛtas tena yenaitad upaśikṣitam / anṛśaṃsās tu kaunteyās tasyādhyakṣān bravīmi vaḥ

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: Yudhishthira, however, known for his righteousness and adherence to Dharma, intervened and stopped Bhima's mocking words.

original: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ kaunteyaṃ bhīmasenam amarṣaṇam / na kālaḥ paruṣasyāyam iti rājābhyabhāṣata

layers.author: km_ganguli
layers.author_bio: An Indian translator known for being the first to provide a complete English translation of the Mahabharata (1883-1896).
layers.content: Yudhishthira emphasized that this was a time for compassion and duty, not for taking revenge or using cruel words against their fallen relatives.
